home.review1: The timed tests helped me become familiar with the real Aptis format, while the detailed review made my mistakes much easier to understand.
home.review2: I like being able to practise on both my laptop and phone. The exercises clearly show which areas need more attention.
home.review3: AptiMate helped me prepare confidently for a computer-based test and improve my Listening and Reading results.
home.review4: The practice flow is clear and close to the real exam. Reviewing every answer helps me improve consistently.
home.review5: Instant results and explanations make it easy to identify weaker skills and save preparation time.
home.review6: The Listening and Reading practice sets are well organised, and the explanations are concise and useful.
home.review7: Realistic timing and clear result pages help me stay focused and monitor my progress.
home.review8: The mobile layout is convenient for quick practice, while full tests on desktop feel close to the real exam.

ui.the_grammar_and_vocabulary_component_is_: The Grammar and Vocabulary component is the core element of the Aptis test. It has two parts, and you will have 25 minutes to complete it.
ui.the_first_part_tests_your_knowledge_of_e: The first part tests your knowledge of English grammar, and the second part focuses on your knowledge of English vocabulary.
ui.the_grammar_and_vocabulary_test_is_marke: The Grammar and Vocabulary test is marked on a scale from 0 to 50. No CEFR level is awarded for this component, but the score is used to assign you to the correct CEFR level for the other skill components.
ui.in_the_grammar_section_you_will_be_prese: In the Grammar section, you will be presented with 25 multiple-choice questions. Complete each sentence by choosing the correct option. Read the whole sentence before choosing your answer.
ui.you_can_flag_questions_you_find_difficul: You can flag questions you find difficult and return to them later in the test.
ui.the_vocabulary_part_also_has_25_question: The Vocabulary part also has 25 questions. There are several question types:
ui.word_definition_match_a_word_to_its_defi: Word definition — match a word to its definition.
ui.word_pairs_match_a_word_to_another_word_: Word pairs — match a word to another word with a very similar meaning.
ui.word_usage_choose_a_word_that_fits_the_c: Word usage — choose a word that fits the context of a sentence.
ui.word_combinations_combine_words_that_are: Word combinations — combine words that are frequently used together.
ui.top_tips_for_the_grammar_and_vocabulary_: Top tips for the Grammar and Vocabulary test
ui.read_all_the_options_before_choosing_you: Read all the options before choosing your answer.
ui.after_choosing_an_option_read_the_senten: After choosing an option, read the sentence again to check your answer before moving on.
ui.do_not_spend_too_long_on_any_question_yo: Do not spend too long on any question. You have to answer 50 questions in 25 minutes. If you cannot think of the answer immediately, continue with the test and return to it later.
ui.improve_your_vocabulary_through_practice: Improve your vocabulary through practice games and activities on the LearnEnglish website.
ui.tips_for_taking_the_aptis_grammar_vocabu: Tips for taking the Aptis Grammar & Vocabulary test

ui.the_aptis_listening_test_consists_of_17_: The Aptis Listening test consists of 17 tasks with a total of 20 questions based on a variety of audio recordings. It focuses on listening skills in real-life situations. Your final score is calculated based on the number of correct answers you provide.
ui.the_questions_in_the_listening_test_are_: The questions in the Listening test are based on four different task types: identifying specific information from short messages or conversations (Part 1), matching information from four speakers talking about the same topic (Part 2), inferring opinions from a conversation between a man and a woman (Part 3), and inferring opinions from longer monologues on a range of topics (Part 4).
ui.you_will_have_approximately_40_minutes_t: You will have approximately 40 minutes to complete the Listening test. Each correct answer is worth one mark, and the total score is converted to the Aptis scale from A1 to C. Each audio recording can be played a maximum of two times.
ui.for_example_to_achieve_a_b2_level_in_the: For example, to achieve a B2 level in the Listening test, you need to reach the required score threshold according to the Aptis scale, demonstrating your ability to process real-life information and infer meaning across a range of contexts.
ui.some_tips_for_taking_the_aptis_listening: Some tips for taking the APTIS Listening test
ui.question_types_in_the_aptis_listening_te: Question types in the APTIS Listening test
ui.the_listening_test_is_relevant_for_both_: The Listening test is relevant for both Aptis and Aptis ESOL. You will need to complete 17 tasks with a total of 20 questions in response to multiple recordings focusing on different aspects of real-life listening.
ui.you_will_listen_to_a_variety_of_recordin: You will listen to a variety of recordings including short messages, dialogues, short monologues and longer monologues. You can hear each recording twice.
ui.these_questions_test_your_ability_to_62e: These questions test your ability to:
ui._identify_specific_information_from_shor: - Identify specific information from short messages or dialogues
ui._match_speakers_to_pieces_of_information: - Match speakers to pieces of information on a common topic
ui._identify_who_expresses_which_opinion_in: - Identify who expresses which opinion in a discussion
ui._identify_a_speaker_s_opinion_or_point_o: - Identify a speaker's opinion or point of view in longer monologues
ui.part_1_information_recognition_you_will_: Part 1 — Information recognition: You will listen to a short message or a dialogue and need to identify specific information such as a phone number, a time or a place.
ui.part_2_information_matching_you_will_lis: Part 2 — Information matching: You will listen to short monologues on a common topic by four different people. You will be asked to match each speaker to a piece of information.
ui.part_3_inference_discussion_you_will_lis: Part 3 — Inference (discussion): You will listen to a man and a woman discuss a topic and express certain opinions. You will be asked to identify who expresses which opinion.
ui.part_4_inference_longer_monologues_you_w: Part 4 — Inference (longer monologues): You will listen to two longer monologues on different topics. You will be asked to identify the speaker's opinion or point of view on two aspects of each topic.

ui.aptis_reading_consists_of_four_tasks_whi: APTIS Reading consists of four tasks which become increasingly difficult as the test progresses. It takes 35 minutes to complete and is designed to assess your ability to read and understand texts in English.

ui.aptis_reading_is_one_of_the_four_compone: APTIS Reading is one of the four components of the APTIS test, developed by the British Council, which is designed to assess a test taker's proficiency in the English language. The APTIS Reading test evaluates your ability to understand and interpret written texts in English across a range of contexts and complexity levels.
ui.the_aptis_reading_test_is_divided_into_f: The APTIS Reading test is divided into four sections, and the tasks become progressively more difficult as the test advances. Unlike a single fixed format, the time allowed varies depending on the version of the test:
ui._part_1_sentence_comprehension_you_will_: - Part 1 – Sentence Comprehension: You will read a short text in the form of a note or an email. For five sentences in the text, you must choose a word to complete each sentence. This part tests your ability to read and understand simple sentences.
ui._part_2_text_cohesion_this_section_conta: - Part 2 – Text Cohesion: This section contains two separate texts. Each text consists of six sentences, but only the first sentence is placed correctly. Your task is to arrange the remaining five sentences in the correct order to form a complete, coherent text.
ui._part_3_opinion_matching_you_will_read_a: - Part 3 – Opinion Matching: You will read a text made up of four paragraphs on a common topic, each paragraph representing a different person's opinions or preferences. You will then match seven given statements to the correct person.
ui._part_4_long_text_comprehension_in_the_f: - Part 4 – Long Text Comprehension: In the final section, you will read a longer text split into seven paragraphs. You are given seven headings and must match one heading to each paragraph.
ui.top_tips_for_the_reading_test_3b9b1b: Top tips for the reading test:
ui._read_all_the_sentences_carefully_first_: - Read all the sentences carefully first, then decide on the correct order. You need to look for words that show how the sentences link with each other.
ui._to_perform_well_in_section_two_first_re: - To perform well in section two, first read each paragraph so you understand each person's point of view. Then read the statements and decide which person's opinion it best represents.
ui._in_section_four_it_is_necessary_to_scro: - In section four it is necessary to scroll the reading text to see all of it. Select the most appropriate heading for each paragraph.
ui._understanding_simple_sentences_and_ever: - Understanding simple sentences and everyday language
ui._recognizing_how_texts_are_structured_an: - Recognizing how texts are structured and how ideas connect
ui._identifying_individual_opinions_and_mat: - Identifying individual opinions and matching them to statements
ui._comprehending_extended_texts_and_identi: - Comprehending extended texts and identifying the main idea of each section

ui.audio_questions_and_task_images_will_be_: Audio, questions and task images will be sent to Groq for transcription and Google Gemini for assessment. Transcripts and feedback are saved with the result. CEFR is an AI estimate, not a certification result; scores out of 50 are for internal practice only. Do not include sensitive personal information in your answers.
ui.you_can_decline_and_return_to_the_test_l: You can decline and return to the test list. For a timed exam, the timer starts when you open the test.
ui.google_gemini_uses_the_free_tier_google_: Google Gemini uses the Free tier: Google may use audio, submitted content and results to improve its products; reviewers may inspect the data. Even fictional answers can identify you through your real voice. Do not send personal, sensitive or confidential information. This feature is for adults aged 18 and over and is unavailable on the Free tier in the EEA, Switzerland or the UK. When quota runs out, requests wait or fail; they do not automatically switch to paid services.

ui.the_aptis_speaking_test_is_assessed_by_e: The Aptis Speaking test is assessed by experienced language experts to ensure objectivity and accuracy. Examiners evaluate your recorded responses against standardized assessment criteria, and their performance is subject to regular quality monitoring and review.
ui.the_speaking_test_consists_of_four_parts: The Speaking test consists of four parts that increase in difficulty, assessing language proficiency from beginner to advanced levels (A1 – C2 on the CEFR scale). Candidates complete the test on a computer, and the total duration is approximately 12 minutes.
ui.your_responses_in_the_speaking_component: Your responses in the Speaking component are assessed against the following criteria:
ui.grammatical_range_and_accuracy_the_abili: Grammatical Range and Accuracy: The ability to use a variety of grammatical structures and appropriate vocabulary accurately.
ui.pronunciation_the_clarity_of_speech_incl: Pronunciation: The clarity of speech, including individual sounds, word stress, and natural intonation.
ui.fluency_the_speed_and_smoothness_of_spee: Fluency: The speed and smoothness of speech, and the ability to link ideas together without excessive hesitation.
ui.task_fulfillment_the_ability_to_address_: Task Fulfillment: The ability to address the prompt effectively, providing relevant answers and developing ideas within the given time limits.
ui.each_part_of_the_speaking_test_focuses_o: Each part of the Speaking test focuses on specific skills, ranging from providing basic personal information to comparing and discussing abstract topics. To find out more about the detailed scoring levels, you can refer to the official AptiMate public band descriptors.

ui.the_aptis_speaking_component_tests_your_: The Aptis Speaking component tests your ability to communicate in English in real-life situations.
ui.it_takes_about_12_minutes_and_it_is_divi: It takes about 12 minutes and it is divided into four sections. Your responses will be recorded and marked by our examiners.
ui.if_you_are_taking_aptis_advanced_you_wil: If you are taking Aptis Advanced, you will have 10 minutes to complete this part.
ui.you_will_be_asked_three_questions_about_: You will be asked three questions about yourself and your interests. You are expected to speak for 30 seconds for each question.
ui.you_will_be_asked_to_describe_a_photogra: You will be asked to describe a photograph, then answer two questions on the topic of the photograph. The questions will ask you to talk about your own experience of the topic and to comment on some more general aspect of the topic. In this part you are expected to speak for 45 seconds for each response.
ui.you_will_be_asked_to_describe_two_photog: You will be asked to describe two photographs, then answer two questions on the topic of the photographs. The questions will ask you to compare some aspect of the topic and to express an opinion on or speculate about the topic. Again, you are expected to speak for 45 seconds for each response.

ui.you_will_be_asked_three_questions_on_a_s: You will be asked three questions on a single topic and given one minute to prepare an answer. You can take brief notes and use these to help structure your answer. You are expected to talk for two minutes.

ui.the_aptis_writing_test_assesses_your_abi: The Aptis Writing test assesses your ability to communicate clearly in written English in real-life situations. The test contains four parts connected by a common topic. You may be asked to join a club, course or community group, respond to other members and write both informal and formal messages.
ui.you_have_50_minutes_to_complete_the_full: You have 50 minutes to complete the full test. All responses are marked by an examiner, so your answers should be relevant, easy to understand and appropriate for the intended reader.
ui.respond_to_five_short_messages_using_a_s: Respond to five short messages using a single word or a short phrase. This part carries fewer marks, so answer accurately without spending too much time on each item.
ui.respond_to_a_request_for_information_in_: Respond to a request for information in complete sentences. Write between 20 and 30 words and focus on relevant content, accurate grammar, punctuation and spelling.
ui.reply_to_three_questions_from_members_of: Reply to three questions from members of a club or group. Write approximately 30 to 40 words for each response and maintain a natural, friendly tone.
ui.write_two_emails_about_the_same_situatio: Write two emails about the same situation. The first is an informal email of 40 to 50 words to a friend. The second is a formal email of 120 to 150 words to a person in authority. Adapt your vocabulary, tone and organisation to each reader.
ui.top_tips_for_the_writing_test_a88985: Top tips for the Writing Test
ui.read_every_task_carefully_and_make_sure_: Read every task carefully and make sure your response covers all requested points. Keep within the recommended word count and leave enough time for the longer tasks in Parts 3 and 4.
ui.use_complete_sentences_where_required_or: Use complete sentences where required, organise longer responses into clear ideas and select an appropriate tone for formal and informal writing. Before submitting, check grammar, spelling, punctuation and whether your message is easy to understand.
